question: What filesystem access-control contract should OpenClaw expose for host file and exec access: a canonical `tools.fs` allow/deny policy, a narrower file-tool-only policy with explicit exec follow-up, or OS/container isolation only?
rationale: This defines a public security boundary and config surface, and current related implementations use competing designs with different exec, migration, and operator-risk tradeoffs.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
options.body: Choose a canonical config shape with deny precedence, path normalization, symlink behavior, fresh/upgrade docs, and an explicit exec scope before landing an implementation.

options.title: Split file tools from exec
options.body: Land file-tool and media path policy only if shell-mediated file access is clearly documented as out of scope and tracked in a narrower exec issue or PR.

options.title: Defer to OS or container isolation
options.body: Decline host path ACL config if maintainers decide OpenClaw should rely on OS users, containers, and the existing workspace-only guard rather than another config boundary.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Choose a canonical config shape with deny precedence, path normalization, symlink behavior, fresh/upgrade docs, and an explicit exec scope before landing an implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combination of prior review context and filesystem-policy/security-boundary history for this public config decision.
